# CAMS 045 Lesson Compiler

Compiles every page of one CAMS 045 Canvas lesson module into a single
reference document, then maps each of that lesson's discussion questions to
the sections that hold the evidence. Everything you need is in this skill and
its three reference files:

- `inputs.md`: what to ask the user for before you start.
- `format-spec.md`: the exact layout of the output document.
- `example-output.md`: a short, made-up excerpt in that layout.

## What you need before you start

**Minimum capability:** a way to read pages from the user's own signed-in
Canvas session. Canvas pages require the user's login, so a plain web request
from your side will not reach them. Use the first of these that you have:

1. **A browser tool that works in the user's signed-in browser** and can read
   the page HTML, not only the visible text. A browser extension provided by
   your AI app is the usual way (Claude in Chrome is one example). Tell the
   user which tool you are using.
2. **The Canvas API through that same session**, if it allows it. For a
   Modules URL like https://canvas.example.edu/courses/123456/modules, the
   module list with items is at
   https://canvas.example.edu/api/v1/courses/123456/modules?include[]=items
   and one page body, as HTML with image alt text, is at
   https://canvas.example.edu/api/v1/courses/123456/pages/page-slug (the slug
   is the last part of the page's address). Replace the example host and
   course number with the ones from the user's Modules URL.
3. **Fallback when you have neither:** ask the user to paste each page's
   content, or to save each page from their browser (Save Page As, which keeps
   the HTML and its alt text) and give you the file. Ask for one page at a
   time, by its exact title.

If none of these works, stop and tell the user. Never guess page content.

You also need a way to create a Word document. If you cannot create files,
give the document as Markdown in the same layout and say so.

## Hard rules (never violated)

- **Never click, open, or interact with anything labeled Quiz, Knowledge Check,
  or Exam.** Read-only navigation only. If a module item's name contains any of
  those words, skip it and list it in the table of contents as
  "(skipped: assessment)".
- **Never submit, answer, or check off anything.** No form fields, no
  discussion posts, no quiz attempts.
- **Never fabricate content.** If a page fails to load or a section is
  unclear, say so in the document rather than guessing or smoothing it over.

## Fidelity rules

- **Copy Canvas text verbatim:** headings, body text, the discussion prompt,
  rubric text, and image descriptions. Copied text is verbatim by default and
  carries no extra label.
- **Mark any paraphrase.** If you shorten or reword anything, put it in a
  paragraph that starts with "Paraphrase:" in italics. Never present a rewrite
  as Canvas's own words.
- **Label outside material.** Facts from your own knowledge or from outside
  Canvas go only in a paragraph that starts with "Outside material (source:
  name the source):" in italics. Never mix them into Canvas text.
- **Never invent missing parts.** If the rubric shows only criterion names,
  points, and rating tiers (for example Excellent, Average, Poor), copy exactly
  that and add no descriptions. If something is missing or will not load,
  write "[Missing in Canvas: what is missing]" at that point.
- **Flag disagreements between sources.** When two places disagree (for
  example the Overview gives one point value and the discussion page or rubric
  gives another), quote both, say where each appears, and list it under
  "Source Conflicts". Do not pick a winner.

## Workflow

### 1. Get the inputs

Ask for everything in `inputs.md` that the user has not already given: the
course Modules URL and the lesson number. Accept "L02", "2", "lesson 2", and
similar, and write the number with two digits.

### 2. Confirm the module

Open the Modules URL. Find the module titled "Lesson NN: ..." and list every
item in it back to the user in one message, marking each assessment that will
be skipped. Wait for the user to confirm it is the right lesson.

### 3. Read every non-assessment item in order

Start with the Overview page (lesson objectives and deliverables; do not skip
it), then follow the module order. For each page:

- **Text:** copy the body verbatim, keeping its heading levels.
- **Images:** capture a description for every image on every page. Canvas
  often keeps the description only in the image's alt attribute, and tools
  that return page text usually drop alt text. Read the alt attribute from
  the page HTML (through your browser tool, the pages API, or a saved page).
  If an image also has a "text description" link or panel, open it and copy
  that text too. If an image has no description anywhere, write
  "[No description in Canvas]".
- **Videos:** decide by page type and content, not by one title pattern. A
  page is a video page when it embeds a player (an iframe or video element,
  for example Kaltura or YouTube), or its title contains the word "Video"
  anywhere ("Video 2.1", "Guest Video", "Video Analysis"). If a page matches
  neither but seems to hold a video (a player area, a "Transcript" link), ask
  the user. For each video, record its exact title as Canvas shows it and its
  position in the sequence. Do not play it or open its transcript panel.

### 4. Collect the discussion assignment

Find the lesson's discussion assignment (in the module or under Assignments,
for example "L02 Analytical Discussion"). Copy verbatim the full prompt: the
questions, the instructions, any passage pasted into the prompt, and the
rubric exactly as Canvas shows it. Read only: do not open the reply box or
post.

### 5. Ask for video transcripts, the one manual step

If the lesson has videos, ask for each transcript by its exact title, one at
a time, in lesson order:

> "This lesson has [N] video(s). Paste the transcript for **[exact video
> title]** whenever you're ready, and I'll put it in the right place."

If the lesson has no videos, skip this step. If the user cannot provide a
transcript, write "[Transcript not provided]" at that video's position.

### 6. Build the document

Follow `format-spec.md` exactly; `example-output.md` shows what it looks
like. Put the compile stamp at the top. Before presenting, reopen or render
the file and check the headings, quotes, and image descriptions.

### 7. Map the discussion questions

For each question in the prompt, name the section or sections that hold the
evidence, by their headings. Keep three cases apart:

- answered by lesson pages (name the page);
- answered only by a passage pasted into the discussion prompt itself (say
  that it is separate from the lesson pages);
- not covered anywhere (say so; do not guess).

Put the map in the "Discussion Question Map" section and also show it in the
chat.

### 8. Present the file

Give the user the file and a short summary: pages compiled, items skipped,
image descriptions captured (a count), source conflicts, and anything
missing. Do not draft the discussion post unless the user asks separately.

## What this skill does not do

- Does not extract video transcripts itself (the user pastes them).
- Does not open, attempt, or submit any quiz, knowledge check, or exam.
- Does not write or submit discussion posts.
- Does not grade or check the user's draft answers against the rubric.

# Compiled reference format

The layout of a CAMS 045 compiled reference, written out so that no earlier
document is needed. Use only the styles named here: Title, Subtitle,
Heading 1 to 3, Normal, and Word's built-in lists. No custom styles.

## Page and file

- US Letter, 1 inch margins.
- File name: CAMS045_L{NN}_Compiled_Reference.docx, where {NN} is the
  two-digit lesson number (L02, L12).

## Top of the document, in this order

1. **Title** (Title style): "CAMS 045 Lesson NN: " followed by the module's
   title exactly as Canvas shows it.
2. **Subtitle** (Subtitle style): "Compiled Reference".
3. **Compile stamp** (Normal, italic), one line: "Compiled YYYY-MM-DD from
   the Canvas Modules URL the user gave, Lesson NN, using the AgentLemon skill
   reference you loaded (for example skill:cams45-selfcontained@1.0.0)."
4. **Contents** (Heading 1 "Contents"): a numbered list of every module item
   in order. Videos end with "(video)". Skipped assessments end with
   "(skipped: assessment)" and appear nowhere else.

## One section per Canvas page

- **Heading 1:** the page title exactly as Canvas shows it, one per page, in
  module order.
- **Heading 2 and Heading 3:** the page's own subheadings, at the same levels
  as on the page. Do not invent headings.
- **Body:** Normal paragraphs, copied verbatim. Keep Canvas bullets and
  numbering as Word lists.
- **Primary-source passages:** a block quote, meaning a Normal paragraph
  indented 0.5 inch on the left, copied verbatim. Put the citation on the next
  line, indented the same way, exactly as Canvas gives it (author, work, and
  line or section).
- **Image descriptions:** inline where the image appears, in square brackets
  and italics: *[Image description: the description text, verbatim]*. Use
  *[No description in Canvas]* when there is none.

## Videos

- Each video gets its own **Heading 1** at its position in the sequence:
  "Video transcript: " followed by the exact video title.
- The transcript follows as Normal paragraphs, verbatim as the user pasted
  it, or *[Transcript not provided]*.

## Labels inside the body

- Verbatim Canvas text carries no label.
- A paraphrase is its own paragraph that starts with *Paraphrase:* in
  italics.
- Outside material is its own paragraph that starts with *Outside material
  (source: name the source):* in italics.
- Anything missing is marked *[Missing in Canvas: what is missing]*.

## End of the document, in this order

1. **Resources Used This Lesson** (Heading 1): copied verbatim from the
   Summary page. Leave the section out if the Summary page lists none.
2. **Source Conflicts** (Heading 1): one bullet per disagreement, quoting
   both sides and naming where each appears, or "None found."
3. **Discussion Question Map** (Heading 1): one Heading 2 per question,
   with the question copied verbatim, then where its evidence is.

# Example output (made up)

A trimmed, invented excerpt that shows the layout in `format-spec.md`. The
lesson, pages, and text are fictional. Style names are shown in square
brackets before each line; they are not part of the text.

---

[Title] CAMS 045 Lesson 99: Rivers and Boundaries

[Subtitle] Compiled Reference

[Normal, italic] *Compiled 2026-01-15 from the Canvas Modules URL the user
gave (https://canvas.example.edu/courses/123456/modules), Lesson 99, using
skill:cams45-selfcontained@1.0.0.*

[Heading 1] Contents

1. Lesson 99 Overview
2. Crossing the River
3. The Ferryman (video)
4. Lesson 99 Knowledge Check (skipped: assessment)
5. Lesson 99 Summary

[Heading 1] Lesson 99 Overview

[Heading 2] Objectives

[Normal] By the end of this lesson you will be able to explain why rivers
mark the edge between two worlds in the stories we read.

[Heading 2] Deliverables

[Normal] Lesson 99 Discussion, 10 points.

[Heading 1] Crossing the River

[Normal] Travelers in these stories must pay to cross, and the price is
always small.

[Normal, indented 0.5 inch] The old man held out his hand and waited, and
no one crossed without paying.

[Normal, indented 0.5 inch] Example Author, Example Poem, lines 1 to 2

[Normal, italic] *[Image description: A small boat on dark water, with a
figure holding a long pole at the back.]*

[Normal, italic] *Outside material (source: the compiler's general
knowledge): Many cultures place a river or sea between the living and the

he asks of travelers.

  Discussion, 10 points"). The discussion page and its rubric say 20 points.

[Heading 1] Discussion Question Map

# Inputs to ask the user for

Ask for anything here that the user has not already given. Never ask for a
password: the user signs in to Canvas in their own browser.

## Before you start (required)

1. **Course Modules URL.** Ask: "What is the address of your CAMS 045 Canvas
   Modules page? Open the course, click Modules, and copy the address bar."
   It looks like https://canvas.example.edu/courses/123456/modules, but the
   host and course number differ by school, section, and semester. Never
   reuse one from an example or an earlier run.
2. **Lesson number.** Accept "L02", "2", or "lesson 2". Write it with two
   digits (02, 12) in titles and the file name.

## Optional

3. **Output format.** A Word document by default. Markdown if the user asks
   or if you cannot create files.

## During the run

4. **Video transcripts,** one at a time, by exact video title, in lesson
   order (step 5 of the skill).
5. **Page content,** only when you are using the paste fallback: one page at
   a time, by exact title.
